answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a stake refundable only through a slow withdrawal queue. Each agent deposits collateral tied to its identity, and refunds are capped per block. An honest agent loses nothing, since the stake returns. An attacker needing N identities must lock N stakes at once and wait out the same queue for each, so cost scales linearly in N while quorum payoff stays fixed. Splitting into fresh keys meets the same limit, and the public queue shows a cluster exiting on one tide. That is the thread binding identity to sunk capital, not cheap keys. No privileged jetty exists.
